_comment: THE CRAB'S CIVICS STAKES, TRANSCRIBED (cultureway phase E4, plan section 2).
platValue (game.js) scores every platform for a voter as SIX coefficient
terms; here it is re-expressed as a LIST of NAMED Layer-1 term-programs.
The platform's value is the SUM of the terms - so the receipt (which term
dominated, read off the largest-magnitude name) and the valuation come from
ONE definition, which is substrate section 3's legibility ruling.
THE READS (PLAT_BUNDLE, game.js): the nine numbers platValue touches, each
an ENGINE call. Two of the underlying helpers - floorBill (a loop over a
payroll) and capStake100 (a loop over the businesses) - are LOOPS, which a
straight-line program cannot express, so the engine computes every helper
in platReads and the term-programs do only the coefficient arithmetic
platValue's own body does, in source order. slot 0 potStake20, 1 pBowls,
2 roofWeight20, 3 roof(0/1), 4 fr, 5 fb, 6 capStake100, 7 purseCost100,
8 pTake.
THE COEFFICIENTS are D/denominator, D = 41,400,000 (game.js): 345000 =
414000 = D/100, 69 = D/(100*6000). floorBill and purseCost SUBTRACT, so
their coefficients are negative and their term bounds go negative - which
the stakes validator permits (a stake term is signed; only the 2^52
magnitude rail applies).
WHAT THE PROOF IS, EXACTLY - and here it IS byte-equality, unlike the E3
depart table's scaled space. Every read platValue touches is an exact
integer, so the summed term value equals the lambda value bit-for-bit on a
(real crab, real platform) grid sweep. MEASURED 2026-08-24 across four
towns (poor + growth, both engines), 205,800 pairs, ZERO mismatches, ZERO
clamps, and every +/-1 coefficient mutation flips hundreds of pairs - so a
wrong coefficient is VISIBLE, the one class of drift E3's scaled space
could not catch. The engine lambda remains the fallback; the grid sweep and
the whole-town election run are the proof.
_ballots_comment: THE BALLOT DIALS, TRANSCRIBED (cultureway phase E4 slice 4a, plan section 2).
The two TOWN-LEVEL dials a mayor sets and a voter prices: WAGE_FLOOR and
HEAD_CAP (game.js). Unlike stakes (per-voter, dispatched on culture), these
are one-per-town facts, so they ride the crab's OWN bundle and adopt IN
PLACE - the WAGE_FLOOR/HEAD_CAP object literals stay as the engine fallback
and floorOf/capOf/allPlatforms read the same steps in the same order
(the E6 crab-as-document idiom, not the slice-3 dispatch).
steps[] IS the ladder (the INDEX is what a save stores, so its meaning is
forever). STEP 0 IS THE FOUNDING POLICY - NO FLOOR / NO LIMIT - what every
pre-feature save loads as (wage:0 / cap:0), and Matt's ruling-4 invariant
(design/cs35-rulings-2026-08-24.md): the ladder EXTENDS, it never deletes
step 0. Byte-equal to the literals by the tabled==literal scenario and the
election A/B; a drifted step names the dial.

_purses_comment: THE FIVE PURSES, TRANSCRIBED (cultureway phase E4 slice 4b, plan section 2;
the tariff joined 2026-08-25 - a duty on the gangway is a fifth answer to
Who pays for the pot - the rate GRID a mayor sets and a voter prices. The
five mechs (levy/dues/rents/tin/tariff) are the engine's own id space (PURSE_KEYS
drives allPlatforms and the levy conflict-of-interest), so they ride the
crab's OWN bundle and adopt IN PLACE beside the ballot dials, the same E6
idiom: the PURSES object literals stay as the engine fallback and purseRate/
purseYield/allPlatforms read the same steps in the same order.
steps[] IS the rate grid; the rate INDEX (0..4, hardcoded in the engine) is
what a save stores, so step 0 is NO TAKE (rate 0 raises nothing) and its
meaning is forever. Byte-equal to the literals by the tabled==literal
scenario and the election A/B. The name/short/unit/who ride the document for
E7's full-crab-document bar; the engine reads the rate grid here (the labels
are byte-equal decoration this slice, exactly as the ballot labels are).

_calendar_relief_comment: THE CALENDAR AND THE RELIEF, TRANSCRIBED (cultureway phase E4 slice 4c).
Unlike the ballot dials and purses (step-ladders a save indexes), these are
SCALAR facts the town runs on - the polling clock and the shelter's terms.
They adopt in place beside the ladders (the E6 idiom): the engine consts
(POLL_WEEKDAY/OPEN/SHUT, SHELTER_RENT/FLOAT/STRIKES/SHUT_NIGHTS, SOUP_MARGIN,
POT_MAX) stay as the fallback, and every reader draws the same scalar.
calendar: pollWeekday is the weekday INDEX (0..6; 6 = Sunday, the town's own
week). pollOpen/pollShut are MINUTES past midnight (7*60 = 420, 19*60 =
1140) - the polls open an hour before the town and shut an hour before it.
relief.soup: potMax is the most bowls a mayor may put on for one night (6);
margin is the shack's margin on a bowl sold to the town, in CENTS (200).
relief.shelter: rent is Mr. Pincherton's nightly charge in CENTS (1000);
float is how many nights of rent the purse carries in hand (1); strikes is
missed nights running before the door is bolted (3); shutNights is how many
nights it stays bolted (4).
THE TRAP THIS FAMILY CARRIES (discipline 5): these sit on STATE and TIME
paths - a pot is SPENT, the shelter CHARGES rent, the door is BOLTED after
strikes and REOPENS after shutNights, the polls OPEN and SHUT on the calendar
day. So the gate is the WHOLE-TOWN run (rent charged, pot bought, door
bolted/reopened), not only a returned number. NOTE potMax is woven into the
stakes lcm denominator (345000 = D/(20*potMax)); transcribing it byte-equal
(=6) is what keeps the stakes exact - a different potMax would silently
desync the platform valuation, which the stakes grid sweep would catch.
_eligibility_comment: THE FRANCHISE, TRANSCRIBED (cultureway phase E4 slice 4d, family 2: who may).
Two PREDICATE programs (0/1) over the persona read bundle (ELIG_BUNDLE,
game.js: npc/owner/homeless), NOT step-tables. Like stakes this is PER-VOTER
- it reads a crab's own attributes - so it dispatches on the voter's culture,
the crab's own (and any culture that declared none) running the engine's own
inlined gates as the byte-equal fallback.
vote: EVERY resident votes (the engine offers the vote errand to every crab
in allCrabs(); the visitor is excluded STRUCTURALLY, not by a predicate), so
the crab program is the constant 1: [PUSHI 1].
stand: only TOWNSFOLK put themselves forward (buildBallot filters c.p.npc;
the player's crew stand only by nomination), so the crab program reads the
npc flag: [LD npc]. Byte-equal to the inlined gates by the staged-election
A/B; a predicate that could return anything but 0/1 is refused by name.
